metadata.note: Q1c (6 marks): gradient S of the T² vs l graph using two well-separated points. Q1d (4 marks): calculate g = 4π²/S. Expected gradient S ≈ 4.0–4.12 s²/m; g ≈ 9.6–9.8 m/s². Follows PHY-JAN23-Q1b (T² table) and the graph plotting Q1b(iii) (not auto-graded).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q1c/d — Gradient and g from Pendulum T² Graph
question.text:
Using the completed T² vs l graph from Table 1 (where T² values range from 0.59 s² at l=0.15 m to 3.06 s² at l=0.75 m), answer the following:

Part (c): Calculate the gradient S of the T² vs l graph. Choose two well-separated points on your best-fit line. (6 marks)

Part (d): Given that S = 4π²/g, calculate the acceleration due to gravity g. (4 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q1c — Gradient:
Using points (0.15, 0.59) and (0.75, 3.06):
S = ΔT²/Δl = (3.06 − 0.59) / (0.75 − 0.15) = 2.47 / 0.60 = 4.12 s² m⁻¹
(Accept any two well-separated, clearly identified points from the best-fit line; S should fall in the range 3.9–4.3)

Q1d — Acceleration due to gravity:
S = 4π²/g → g = 4π²/S = 4 × 9.870 / 4.12 = 39.48 / 4.12 ≈ 9.58 m s⁻²
(Accept any answer in range 9.2–10.2 m s⁻², depending on gradient chosen)

Gradient formula: S = ΔT²/Δl (rise over run from two distant points on best-fit line)
Q1c — Calculate the gradient S of the T² vs l graph using two well-separated points. (6 marks)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Δl = the difference in l values for your two chosen points on the line of best fit.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: S = ΔT² ÷ Δl = 2.47 ÷ 0.60 = 4.12 s²/m. Divide the change in T² by the change in l.
